note: One narrow idea per Short. Public-domain book; hooks and examples in our own modern words.

episodes.title: Your beliefs have a motive
episodes.hook: Your strongest beliefs might just be your wishes in disguise.
episodes.angle: Philosophies often justify what their makers already wanted. Example: someone who 'believes' all rich people are evil right after failing a business.

episodes.title: Truth isn't always nice
episodes.hook: Why do you assume the truth will make you feel good?
episodes.angle: We prefer comfortable lies; a free mind can handle unpleasant truths. Example: asking a friend for honest feedback and actually wanting it.

episodes.title: Free spirits
episodes.hook: If all your opinions match your friends', are they really yours?
episodes.angle: A free spirit thinks differently from what their background expects. Example: the kid who questions the family religion or politics, respectfully.

episodes.title: Convictions are prisons
episodes.hook: The person who never changes their mind has stopped thinking.
episodes.angle: Fixed convictions can block truth more than lies. Example: someone defending a team or brand no matter what.

episodes.title: Herd morality
episodes.hook: The crowd calls whatever is safe for the crowd 'good'.
episodes.angle: Much morality protects the average from the exceptional. Example: the student mocked for studying because it makes others look bad.

episodes.title: Madness of groups
episodes.hook: Madness is rare in people. In groups, it's the rule.
episodes.angle: Crowds lose the sense individuals have. Example: a comment section piling on someone over a misunderstanding.

episodes.title: Standing out costs
episodes.hook: Being yourself will cost you some people. Pay it.
episodes.angle: Independence means accepting loneliness at times. Example: leaving the friend group that only gossips.

episodes.title: Don't fight monsters badly
episodes.hook: If you fight monsters, be careful not to become one.
episodes.angle: Fighting evil can turn you into it. Example: someone exposing a bully online who starts bullying too.

episodes.title: Stare into the abyss
episodes.hook: When you stare into the abyss, it stares back.
episodes.angle: What you focus on shapes you. Example: doomscrolling bad news until you see the world as only bad.

episodes.title: What doesn't kill you
episodes.hook: Pain is not proof you're failing. It might be proof you're growing.
episodes.angle: Hardship can strengthen a person who chooses to use it. Example: a lifter's sore muscles, a breakup that made someone kinder.

episodes.title: Comfort makes you small
episodes.hook: Your comfort zone is slowly making you smaller.
episodes.angle: Avoiding all difficulty weakens a person. Example: someone who stops ordering food by phone because texting is easier, then can't call at all.

episodes.title: Become who you are
episodes.hook: You're not meant to find yourself. You're meant to create yourself.
episodes.angle: Identity is made through choices, not discovered. Example: someone who 'isn't creative' until they draw every day for a year.

episodes.title: Masters and slaves of values
episodes.hook: Are your values yours, or did someone hand them to you?
episodes.angle: Some values are created out of strength, others out of resentment. Example: calling success 'shallow' only after missing it.

episodes.title: Envy disguised as virtue
episodes.hook: Sometimes 'I'd never want that' really means 'I can't have that'.
episodes.angle: Resentment dresses itself up as moral superiority. Example: mocking the gym-goer while secretly wishing you went.

episodes.title: Live dangerously
episodes.hook: Build your house on the slopes of a volcano.
episodes.angle: A meaningful life requires risk. Example: quitting the safe but dead-end job to try the thing you care about.
